h1: Occupational Driver's License (ODL) Lawyer El Paso, TX
intro: A suspended Texas license does not have to mean losing your job. Under Transportation Code Chapter 521, Subchapter L, a court can grant an occupational driver's license that lets you drive to work, school and essential errands while the suspension runs. Attorney Robert Navar prepares and files the petition in El Paso County.
summaryHeading: Suspended license, but you still have to get to work
summary: An occupational driver's license (ODL) is a court-ordered restricted license for a person whose Texas license is suspended — commonly after a DWI-related suspension or repeated moving-violation convictions — allowing driving for work, school and household needs.

The ODL is obtained by filing a petition in an El Paso County court with an SR-22 insurance certificate and a certified driving record; the judge's signed order serves as your license for a limited time while DPS issues the card.
The order restricts when, where and why you may drive — the hours per day, the counties, and the purposes — based on what you ask for and what the judge approves.
An ODL will not fix an OMNI hold or an expired license — those are fixed by clearing the tickets. We check which problem you actually have at a free consultation. Call 915-503-1600.

sections.heading: Suspension or Hold? Why the Answer Decides Everything
paragraphs: Transportation Code Chapter 521, Subchapter L lets a court grant an occupational license to a person whose license has been suspended or revoked and who needs to drive for work, education or essential household duties. In El Paso the typical client has an administrative or court suspension after a DWI arrest, a suspension tied to driving without insurance, or a suspension DPS imposed after repeated moving-violation convictions. Texas no longer uses the former Driver Responsibility Program points system, but repeated convictions can still affect a driver's record and may lead to suspension in some circumstances.

Not every suspension qualifies. In general an ODL is not available when the license was suspended for a medical reason or for failure to pay child support, and some DWI histories carry statutory waiting periods. We review your DPS record at the consultation and tell you plainly whether an ODL appears to be available and when.

One distinction comes first: a suspension is different from an OMNI hold. If DPS is refusing to renew your license because of unresolved tickets, you need the tickets cleared, not an ODL. If DPS has actively suspended your driving privilege, an ODL is the tool. Many clients have both, and we address them in the right order.

sections.heading: Where the Petition Is Filed and What It Has to Say
paragraphs: An occupational license is granted by a court order, not by DPS. Depending on the type of suspension, the petition is filed in a justice court, county court or district court in El Paso County — the Justice of the Peace precincts see many of them — or, for a DWI-related suspension, generally in the court that heard the criminal case. The petition is a sworn document that sets out why the suspension happened, why you need to drive, where you work or attend school, and the specific hours, days, routes and counties you are asking for.

A letter from your employer confirming your schedule, a class schedule from UTEP or EPCC, and proof of insurance all strengthen the request. For Fort Bliss soldiers we include the duty schedule; for drivers who work across county lines we address that specifically, because the order only authorizes driving where it says.
Robert Navar drafts the petition and proposed order, files it, and sets it for the judge. We attend any hearing with you.

sections.heading: The SR-22 and the Rest of the Packet
paragraphs: Before the judge signs, you must show financial responsibility with an SR-22 — a certificate your insurer files with DPS confirming you carry at least the state minimum liability coverage. Most carriers in El Paso can issue one for a fee, and drivers who do not own a car can buy a non-owner SR-22 policy. In general the SR-22 must stay in force for the life of the occupational license; if it lapses, the ODL can be cancelled.

You will also need a certified copy of your driving record from DPS, any required DWI education or ignition interlock documentation when the suspension stems from a DWI, and payment of the court filing fee and the DPS license fee, both set by the court and DPS. We walk you through each item so the petition is complete the first time.

sections.heading: Hours, Counties and Purposes: Reading the Order You Will Carry
paragraphs: An occupational license is restricted by design. Under Transportation Code §521.248 the order may not authorize more than four hours of driving in any 24-hour period unless the court finds a necessity, in which case it may allow up to 12 hours, and the judge sets the days, times and purposes — commonly work, school, medical appointments, church and essential errands like groceries and childcare. The order names the counties where you may drive, so an El Paso order can reach neighboring counties if your work takes you there and the judge agrees. DWI-related suspensions may carry additional conditions such as an interlock device.

Once the judge signs, the order and the SR-22 go to DPS with the fee. Under the statute the signed court order itself serves as your license for a limited period while DPS issues the occupational license card. Keep a copy in the vehicle.

Driving outside the hours, counties or purposes in the order is treated like driving without a valid license, and it can lead to a driving while license invalid charge and loss of the ODL. We write the request as broadly as your facts support.

sections.heading: Fees, Timing, and the Tickets Behind the Suspension
paragraphs: The total cost of an ODL has three parts: our attorney fee, quoted flat at the free consultation based on the type of suspension; the court filing fee; and the DPS occupational license fee. The SR-22 is paid to your insurer. How long the process takes depends mostly on how quickly the driving record and SR-22 arrive and when the court can take up the petition; timing cannot be promised, and DWI cases can take longer because of statutory waiting periods.

Many El Paso suspensions start with tickets, and that is where we can often save you the most. If the convictions behind a suspension are still pending cases, pursuing a dismissal or deferred disposition may keep the record from getting worse. A DWLI or no driver's license ticket needs its own defense, which we handle for a flat $59–$69. Our free ticket and warrant lookup finds every open case first.

faqs.q: What is an occupational driver's license in Texas?
faqs.a: It is a restricted license authorized by Transportation Code Chapter 521, Subchapter L, granted by court order to a person whose regular license is suspended. It allows driving for work, school and essential household purposes within the hours, counties and conditions the judge sets.

faqs.q: Can I get an ODL for any suspension?
faqs.a: No. ODLs are commonly available for DWI-related suspensions and suspensions tied to driving-record or insurance problems. In general they are not available for medical or child-support suspensions, and some DWI histories carry waiting periods. We review your DPS record before filing.

faqs.q: Do I need an SR-22 for an occupational license?
faqs.a: Yes. An SR-22 is a certificate of financial responsibility your insurer files with DPS. It generally must be in place before the judge signs the order and must stay active for the term of the ODL, or the license can be cancelled.

faqs.q: How many hours a day can I drive on an ODL?
faqs.a: The statute caps the daily hours an order may authorize, and the judge sets the specific days, times and purposes within that cap based on what you show you need. We draft the request to match your actual work and school schedule.

faqs.q: How long does it take to get an occupational license in El Paso?
faqs.a: It depends on how quickly the certified driving record and SR-22 arrive and when the court can take up the petition. Timing cannot be promised. Once signed, the order lets you drive for a limited period while DPS prints the card.

faqs.q: DPS won't renew my license. Do I need an ODL?
faqs.a: Often not. A renewal denial usually points to an OMNI hold from unresolved tickets, which is fixed by clearing those cases, not by an ODL. See our OMNI hold removal page, or call us and we will tell you which problem you have.
